label: ass:continuous-paths
body_md:
\label{ass:continuous-paths}
  The sample paths \(t \mapsto X(t)\) are continuous almost surely.
head: environment

title: Theorem
body_md: Under \(H_0\), \(\lim_{n\to\infty}\Pi_n(H_1|X_{1:n}) = 0\) a.s.\ \raisebox{.25pt}{\([\mathbb{P}_0^\infty]\)}.
head: environment

label: ass:compact-support-tau
body_md:
\label{ass:compact-support-tau}
  The prior measure on the time instants, \(\Pi_\tau(\cdot|p)\), is supported on a compact subset \(\mathcal C_p\subset \mathcal T_p\), that is, \(\Pi_\tau(\mathcal C_p|p)=1\) for all \(p\) such that \(\Pi(p)>0\).
head: environment

label: ass:prior-p-finite
body_md:
\label{ass:prior-p-finite}
  The prior \(\Pi(p)\) has finite support, i.e., \(\Pi(p) = 0\) for all \(p > P_{\max}\).
head: environment

label: th:consistency-rates-h0
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{th:consistency-rates-h0}
  Suppose~\ref{ass:continuous-paths}--\ref{ass:prior-p-finite} hold. Then, \(\Pi_n(H_1|X_{1:n}) = O_{\mathbb{P}_0}(n^{-p_{\min}/2})\) under \(H_0\).
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: If \(p_{\min}=1\) we recover the standard parametric rate \(n^{-1/2}\). Even though the asymptotic rate \(O_{\mathbb{P}_0}(n^{-p_{\min}/2})\) would suggest that it is better to ignore low values of \(p\) in the prior to improve consistency speed, finite-sample performance can be hurt by considering many components, since they introduce increasingly high collinearity. Moreover, removing low-dimensional alternatives makes the test more conservative and reduces interpretability.
head: environment

label: ass:positive-prior-mass
body_md:
\label{ass:positive-prior-mass}
  The prior distribution \(\Pi\) charges open sets, i.e., \(\Pi(p)>0\) for all \(p\in\mathbb{N}\) and \(\Pi_{\tau,b}^{\text{slab}}(U|p)>0\) for all open sets \(U \subseteq \mathcal T_p\times \mathbb{R}^p\), where \(\Pi_{\tau,b}^{\text{slab}}(\cdot|p)\) is the slab part of the joint prior measure on \((\tau, b)\).
head: environment

label: th:consistency-rates-h1
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{th:consistency-rates-h1}
  Suppose~\ref{ass:continuous-paths} and~\ref{ass:positive-prior-mass} hold. Then, \(\Pi_n(H_0|X_{1:n}) = O_{\mathbb{P}_{\mu_*}}(e^{-n\gamma})\) under \(H_1\), for any \(0 < \gamma < \frac{1}{2}\|\mu_*\|^2_K\).
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: The upper bound on \(\gamma\) is not arbitrary; we will show in Section~\ref{sec:optimality} that it is in fact an information-theoretic limit. We also note that, as expected, the rate will be faster when it is easier to distinguish \(\mu_*\) from the zero function, that is, the larger \(\|\mu_*\|_K\) is.
head: environment

label: ass:positive-prior-mass-alt
body_md:
\label{ass:positive-prior-mass-alt}
  There exists \(\theta_0=(p_0,\tau_0,b_0)\) such that \(p_0\leq P_{\max}\), \(\tau_0\in \mathcal C_{p_0}\), \(b_0\in\mathbb{R}^{p_0} \setminus \{0\}\) and \(\|\mu_* - \mu_{\theta_0}\|^2_K < \|\mu_*\|^2_K\). Moreover, for each \(p\leq P_{\max}\) we have \(\Pi(p)>0\) and \(\Pi_{\tau,b}^{\text{slab}}(\cdot|p)\) has full support on \(\mathcal C_p \times \mathbb{R}^p\).
head: environment

label: th:consistency-rates-h1-alt
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{th:consistency-rates-h1-alt}
  Suppose~\ref{ass:continuous-paths}--\ref{ass:prior-p-finite} and~\ref{ass:positive-prior-mass-alt} hold. Then, \(\Pi_n(H_0|X_{1:n}) = O_{\mathbb{P}_{\mu_*}}(e^{-n\gamma})\) under \(H_1\), for any \(0 < \gamma < \frac{1}{2}(\|\mu_*\|^2_K - \|\mu_* - \mu_{\theta_0}\|^2_K)\).
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: By considering~\ref{ass:positive-prior-mass-alt} instead of~\ref{ass:positive-prior-mass} we gain a simpler condition that does not conflict with the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{th:consistency-rates-h0}, but the price we pay is a slower contraction rate under \(H_1\) (unless \(\mu_* \in \mathcal{H}_0(K)\)). Moreover, even though~\ref{ass:positive-prior-mass-alt} can be satisfied with just \(p_0=1\), the rate improves with the quality of the approximation (i.e.\ when \(\|\mu_* - \mu_{\theta_0}\|^2_K\) is small), so we can expect much faster rates if the condition holds for bigger values of \(p_0\).
head: environment

label: ass:uniform-consistency-plug-in
body_md:
\label{ass:uniform-consistency-plug-in}
  For every \(p\) with \(\Pi(p)>0\) and any compact set \(\mathcal C_p\subset \mathcal T_p\), it holds that
  \[
  \sup_{\tau\in \mathcal C_p}\|\hat K_{n,\tau} - K_\tau\| \stackrel{\mathbb{P}}{\longrightarrow} 0.
  \]
head: environment

label: prop:sample-cov-matrix-convergence
title: Proposition
head: environment

label: th:consistency-rates-h0-plugin
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{th:consistency-rates-h0-plugin}
  Suppose~\ref{ass:continuous-paths}--\ref{ass:prior-p-finite} and~\ref{ass:uniform-consistency-plug-in} hold. Then, \(\hat \Pi_n(H_1|X_{1:n}) = O_{\mathbb{P}_0}(n^{-p_{\min}/2})\) under \(H_0\).
head: environment

label: th:consistency-rates-h1-plugin
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{th:consistency-rates-h1-plugin}
  Suppose~\ref{ass:continuous-paths},~\ref{ass:positive-prior-mass} and~\ref{ass:uniform-consistency-plug-in} hold. Then, \(\hat \Pi_n(H_0|X_{1:n}) = O_{\mathbb{P}_{\mu_*}}(e^{-n\gamma})\) under \(H_1\), for any \(0<\gamma<\frac{1}{2}\|\mu_*\|_K^2\). Alternatively, if~\ref{ass:continuous-paths}--\ref{ass:prior-p-finite},~\ref{ass:positive-prior-mass-alt} and~\ref{ass:uniform-consistency-plug-in} hold, then \(\hat \Pi_n(H_0|X_{1:n}) = O_{\mathbb{P}_{\mu_*}}(e^{-n\gamma})\) under \(H_1\), for any \(0<\gamma<\frac{1}{2}(\|\mu_*\|_K^2 - \|\mu_* - \mu_{\theta_0}\|_K^2)\).
head: environment

label: prop:optimality-rates-h1
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:optimality-rates-h1}
  There is no \(\zeta > \frac{1}{2}\|\mu_*\|_K^2\) such that \(\Pi_n(H_0|X_{1:n}) = O_{\mathbb{P}_{\mu_*}}(e^{-n\zeta})\) under \(H_1\).
head: environment

title: Proof\
body_md:
Under~\ref{ass:compact-support-tau} and~\ref{ass:prior-p-finite}, the sum \(m_1(X_{1:n})\) simplifies to
  \[
  m_1(X_{1:n}) = \sum_{p=p_{\min}}^{P_{\max}} \Pi(p) I_{n,p}(\mathcal C_p).
  \]

  Fix \(p_{\min} \leq p\leq P_{\max}\) and let \(\varepsilon>0\). Note that the minimum eigenvalue function \(\tau\mapsto\lambda_{\min}(K_\tau)\) is continuous by Weyl's inequality \citep[Theorem~VI.2.1]{bhatia1996matrix} and the continuity of \(K\). Because \(\mathcal C_p\) is compact and \(K_\tau\) is strictly positive definite, there exists \(\lambda_p>0\) with
  \[
  \lambda_{\min}(K_\tau)\ge \lambda_p>0\quad\text{for all }\tau\in \mathcal C_p.
  \]
  Since \(\Lambda_\tau = nK_\tau + \eta^{-2}I_p\), this implies that \(\lambda_{\min}(\Lambda_\tau) = n\lambda_{\min}(K_\tau) + \eta^{-2} \geq n\lambda_p>0\) for all \(\tau \in \mathcal C_p\). Therefore, the following holds for all \(\tau\in \mathcal C_p\):
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item[(i)] \(|\Lambda_\tau| \geq (n\lambda_p)^p\).
    \item[(ii)] \(v'\Lambda_{\tau}^{-1}v \leq \frac{1}{n\lambda_p}\|v\|^2\) for any \(v\neq 0\).
  \end{enumerate}
  Only the second assertion deserves a comment: the Rayleigh quotient of a symmetric matrix is bounded above by its maximum eigenvalue \citep[Theorem 4.2.2]{horn1985matrix}, and we have \(\lambda_{\max}(\Lambda_\tau^{-1})=(\lambda_{\min}(\Lambda_\tau))^{-1}\). Combining (i), (ii) and~\eqref{eq:m-slab} yields the upper bound
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:upper-bound-m-slab}
  m_{\text{slab}}(X_{1:n}|p,\tau) \leq \eta^{-p}(n\lambda_p)^{-p/2} \exp\left\{\frac{1}{2n\lambda_p}\|S_n(\tau)\|^2\right\}, \quad \text{for all } \tau \in \mathcal C_p.
  \end{equation}

  Now define \(Z_\tau = S_n(\tau)/\sqrt{n}\) for each \(\tau\), and note that \(Z_\tau \sim \mathcal N_p(0, K_\tau)\) under \(H_0\), so its distribution is independent of \(n\). Since
  \[
  \sup_{\tau \in \mathcal C_p} \frac{\|S_n(\tau)\|^2}{n} = \sup_{\tau \in \mathcal C_p} \|Z_\tau\|^2,
  \]
  we consider for any \(M>0\) the \(\mathbb{P}_0\)-measurable event
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:event-E-n-M}
  E_{M} = \left\{\sup_{\tau\in \mathcal C_p} \|Z_\tau\|^2\leq M\right\}.
  \end{equation}
  The map \(\tau \mapsto Z_\tau(\omega)\) is continuous for almost every \(\omega\) by~\ref{ass:continuous-paths}, so on the compact set \(\mathcal C_p\) and the points of continuity in \(\omega\), the continuous function \(\tau \mapsto \|Z_\tau(\omega)\|^2\) attains its supremum. Hence, \(\sup_{\tau \in \mathcal C_p} \|Z_\tau\|^2 < \infty\) almost surely, which trivially implies that we can choose \(M\) large enough so that the complement \(E_{M}^c\) is negligible in probability, say \(\mathbb{P}_0(E_{M}^c) < \varepsilon\).

  On the other hand, on \(E_{M}\) the upper bound in~\eqref{eq:upper-bound-m-slab} reduces to the deterministic bound
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:deterministic-bound-sup-mslab}
  \sup_{\tau \in \mathcal C_p} m_{\text{slab}}(X_{1:n}|p,\tau) \leq \eta^{-p}(n\lambda_p)^{-p/2}\exp\left\{\frac{M}{2\lambda_p}\right\}.
  \end{equation}
  Since \(\Pi_\tau(\mathcal C_p|p)= 1\), by~\eqref{eq:deterministic-bound-sup-mslab} we have (still on the event \(E_{M}\))
  \[
  I_{n,p}(\mathcal C_p)\leq \sup_{\tau\in\mathcal C_p} m_{\text{slab}}(X_{1:n}|p,\tau) \int_{\mathcal C_p} \Pi(\tau|p)\, d\tau \leq Dn^{-p/2},
  \]
  where \(D>0\) is a constant independent of \(n\). Hence, for sufficiently large \(n\) we have
  \[
  \mathbb{P}_0(I_{n,p}(\mathcal C_p) > Dn^{-p/2}) \leq \mathbb{P}_0(E_{M}^c ) < \varepsilon,
  \]
  so \(I_{n,p}(\mathcal C_p)=O_{\mathbb{P}_0}(n^{-p/2})\). Write \(I_{n,p}(\mathcal C_p)=n^{-p/2}Y_{n,p}\), where \(Y_{n,p}=O_{\mathbb{P}_0}(1)\) by definition. Then, because the dominant term in the finite sum \(m_1(X_{1:n})\) is the first term, we have
  \[
  m_1(X_{1:n}) = \sum_{p=p_{\min}}^{P_{\max}} \Pi(p) n^{-p/2}Y_{n,p} = O_{\mathbb{P}_0}(n^{-p_{\min}/2}).
  \]
  Lastly, note that
  \[
  \Pi_n(H_1|X_{1:n}) \leq \frac{1-\pi_0}{\pi_0}m_1(X_{1:n}),
  \]
  so by the continuous mapping theorem the stochastic bound translates immediately and \(\Pi_n(H_1|X_{1:n})=O_{\mathbb{P}_0}(n^{-p_{\min}/2})\), as claimed.
head: environment

label: eq:approximation-property-mu
title: Proof\
body_md:
The RKHS framework will allow us to work, via a suitable approximation, in a finite-dimensional setting. First, since \(\mathcal{H}_0(K)\) is dense in \(\mathcal{H}(K)\), for any \(\varepsilon>0\) there exists a parameter \(\theta_\varepsilon = (p_\varepsilon, \tau_\varepsilon, b_\varepsilon)\) such that
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:approximation-property-mu}
  \|\mu_* - \mu_{\tau_\varepsilon, b_\varepsilon}\|_K < \varepsilon,
  \end{equation}
  where \(\mu_{\tau_\varepsilon, b_\varepsilon}\) is shorthand for \(\mu_{\theta_\varepsilon}\). Since \(\mu_* \neq 0\), choosing \(\varepsilon\) small enough (e.g.\ \(\varepsilon\leq\|\mu_*\|_K\)) guarantees that \(\mu_{\tau_\varepsilon, b_\varepsilon}\neq 0\), and hence \(b_\varepsilon \neq 0\). By~\ref{ass:positive-prior-mass}, \(\Pi(p_\varepsilon)>0\) and there exists a neighborhood \(U =U_1 \times U_2\) of \((\tau_\varepsilon, b_\varepsilon)\) within \(\mathcal T_{p_\varepsilon}\times \mathbb{R}^{p_\varepsilon}\) with positive prior probability. We can (and do) take \(U_1\) and \(U_2\) compact, and arrange \(0\notin U_2\). 
  
  Let \((\tau, b)\in U\) and define \(\mu_*(\tau) = (\mu_*(t_1), \dots, \mu_*(t_{p_\varepsilon}))'\) and \(Z_\tau = (S_n(\tau) - n\mu_*(\tau))/\sqrt{n}\). Note that \(Z_\tau\sim \mathcal N_{p_\varepsilon}(0, K_\tau)\) under \(H_1\), so its distribution is independent of \(n\). Substituting in~\eqref{eq:likelihood} yields
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:log-likelihood-H1}
  \log L(X_{1:n}|p_\varepsilon, \tau, b) = n\mu_*(\tau)'b - \frac{n}{2}b'K_\tau b + \sqrt{n}Z_\tau'b.
  \end{equation}
  On the one hand, for \((\tau, b)\in U\) define the function
  \[
  f(\tau, b) = \mu_*(\tau)'b - \frac{1}{2}b'K_\tau b = \mu_*(\tau)'b - \frac{1}{2}\|\mu_{\tau,b}\|^2_K,
  \]
  and observe that by the reproducing property and the linearity of the inner product we have
  \[
  \left\langle\mu_*,\mu_{\tau, b}\right\rangle_K = \left\langle\mu_*,\ \sum_{j=1}^{p_\varepsilon} \beta_j K(t_j, \cdot)\right\rangle_K = \sum_{j=1}^{p_\varepsilon} \beta_j \left\langle\mu_*,K(t_j, \cdot)\right\rangle_K = \mu_*(\tau)'b.
  \]
  Thus, using the familiar identity \(\|f-g\|^2 = \|f\|^2 + \|g\|^2 - 2\left\langlef,g\right\rangle\), we can write
  \[
  f(\tau, b) = \left\langle\mu_*,\mu_{\tau, b}\right\rangle_K - \frac{1}{2}\|\mu_{\tau,b}\|^2_K = \frac{1}{2}\|\mu_*\|^2_K - \frac{1}{2}\|\mu_* - \mu_{\tau, b}\|^2_K.
  \]
  Moreover, by the triangle inequality we have
  \[
  \|\mu_* - \mu_{\tau, b}\|_K \leq \|\mu_* - \mu_{\tau_\varepsilon, b_\varepsilon}\|_K + \|\mu_{\tau_\varepsilon, b_\varepsilon} - \mu_{\tau,b}\|_K.
  \]
  Then, by~\eqref{eq:approximation-property-mu} and the continuity of the map \((\tau, b) \mapsto \mu_{\tau, b}\) in the RKHS norm (which follows from the continuity of \(K\)), after shrinking \(U\) if necessary we have \(\|\mu_* - \mu_{\tau,b}\|_K < 2\varepsilon\) for all \((\tau,b)\in U\). Consequently,
  \[
  f(\tau, b) \geq \frac{1}{2}\|\mu_*\|^2_K - 2\varepsilon^2 =: c_\varepsilon > 0,
  \]
  where positivity holds by choosing \(\varepsilon\) small enough. On the other hand, note that by the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality
  \[
  \sqrt{n} Z_\tau'b \geq \sqrt{n}\cdot \inf_{b\in U_2} Z_\tau'b \geq -\sqrt{n}\cdot \sup_{b\in U_2} \|b\|\cdot \sup_{\tau \in U_1}\|Z_\tau\|.
  \]

  All in all, we see from~\eqref{eq:log-likelihood-H1} that for all \((\tau, b)\in U\) we obtain a uniform lower bound for the log-likelihood given by
  \[
  \log L(X_{1:n}|p_\varepsilon, \tau, b) = nf(\tau, b) +  \sqrt{n}Z_\tau'b \geq nc_\varepsilon - \sqrt{n}B\cdot \sup_{\tau\in U_1}\|Z_\tau\|,
  \]
  where \(B=\sup_{b\in U_2} \|b\|\) satisfies \(0 < B < \infty\), since \(U_2\) is a compact set with \(0\notin U_2\). Hence, by~\eqref{eq:posterior-slab-m1} and~\eqref{eq:m-slab}, we have
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:lower-bound-m1}
    \begin{split}
    m_1(X_{1:n}) &\geq \Pi(p_\varepsilon) \int_{U_1} \int_{U_2} \mathcal N_{p_\varepsilon}(b|0, \eta^2 I_{p_\varepsilon}) \exp\left\{nf(\tau, b) +  \sqrt{n}Z_\tau'b\right\}\Pi(\tau|p_{\varepsilon})\, db\, d\tau \\
    &\geq D \exp\left\{nc_\varepsilon - \sqrt{n}B\cdot \sup_{\tau\in U_1}\|Z_\tau\|\right\},
    \end{split}
  \end{equation}
  where \(D=\Pi(p_\varepsilon)\Pi_\tau(U_1|p_{\varepsilon})\Pi_b^{\text{slab}}(U_2|p_{\varepsilon})>0\) by assumption. Next, note that \(\sup_{\tau\in U_1}\|Z_\tau\|\) is \(O_{\mathbb{P}_{\mu_*}}(1)\) (by the same argument as in the proof of Theorem~\ref{th:consistency-rates-h0}), so for all \(\delta>0\) there exists \(M>0\) such that \(\mathbb{P}_{\mu_*}(B\cdot \sup_{\tau\in U_1} \|Z_\tau\| \geq M) < \delta\). Thus, by~\eqref{eq:lower-bound-m1} we get
  \[
  \mathbb{P}_{\mu_*}(m_1(X_{1:n}) \leq D \exp\{nc_\varepsilon - \sqrt{n}M\}) \leq  \mathbb{P}_{\mu_*}\left(B\cdot \sup_{\tau\in U_1} \|Z_\tau\| \geq M\right) < \delta.
  \]
  Since \(nc_\varepsilon/(1+\varepsilon)\) grows slower than \(nc_\varepsilon - \sqrt{n}M\) as \(n\to\infty\), for sufficiently large \(n\) we get the probability bound
  \[
  \mathbb{P}_{\mu_*}\left(m_1(X_{1:n}) \leq D \exp\{nc_\varepsilon/(1+\varepsilon)\}\right) \leq \mathbb{P}_{\mu_*}\left(m_1(X_{1:n}) \leq D \exp\{nc_\varepsilon - \sqrt{n}M\}\right) < \delta.
  \]
  To conclude, observe that by~\eqref{eq:posterior-slab}
  \[
  \Pi_n(H_0|X_{1:n}) = \frac{\pi_0}{\pi_0 + (1-\pi_0)m_1(X_{1:n})} \leq \frac{\pi_0}{(1-\pi_0)m_1(X_{1:n})},
  \]
  so if we define \(\tilde{D}=\pi_0/((1-\pi_0)D)\), for large \(n\) we have
  \[
  \mathbb{P}_{\mu_*}\left(\Pi_n(H_0|X_{1:n}) > \tilde{D}\exp\left\{\frac{-nc_\varepsilon}{1+\varepsilon}\right\}\right) \leq \mathbb{P}_{\mu_*}\left(m_1(X_{1:n}) \leq D \exp\left\{\frac{nc_\varepsilon}{1+\varepsilon}\right\}\right) < \delta,
  \]
  i.e., \(\Pi_n(H_0|X_{1:n}) = O_{\mathbb{P}_{\mu_*}}(e^{-nc_\varepsilon/(1+\varepsilon)})\). Since \(\varepsilon\) was arbitrarily small, the constant \(\gamma\) in the exponent is as close as desired to \(\lim_{\varepsilon\to 0}\, c_\varepsilon/(1+\varepsilon)=\frac{1}{2}\|\mu_*\|^2_K\).

title: Proof\
body_md:
By~\ref{ass:positive-prior-mass-alt}, there exist \(p_0\leq P_{\max}\), \(\tau_0\in \mathcal C_{p_0}\), and \(b_0\in\mathbb{R}^{p_0}\setminus\{0\}\) such that
  \[
  \xi:=\|\mu_*-\mu_{\tau_0,b_0}\|_K < \|\mu_*\|_K.
  \]
  By the full support condition in~\ref{ass:positive-prior-mass-alt}, there exists a compact neighborhood \(U=U_1\times U_2\) of \((\tau_0,b_0)\) within \(\mathcal C_{p_0}\times\mathbb{R}^{p_0}\setminus\{0\}\) with \(\Pi(p_0)\Pi_\tau(U_1|p_0)\Pi_b^{\text{slab}}(U_2|p_0)>0\). Let \((\tau,b)\in U\) and define \(f(\tau, b)\) as in the proof of Theorem~\ref{th:consistency-rates-h1}, i.e.,
  \[
  f(\tau, b) = \frac{1}{2}\|\mu_*\|_K^2 - \frac{1}{2}\|\mu_* - \mu_{\tau, b}\|_K^2.
  \]
  Let \(\varepsilon >0\) be small enough so that \(\xi + \varepsilon < \|\mu_*\|_K\). By shrinking \(U\) we can ensure that \(\|\mu_{\tau_0,b_0}-\mu_{\tau,b}\|_K < \varepsilon\), and then by the triangle inequality we have \(\|\mu_*-\mu_{\tau,b}\|_K \leq \xi + \varepsilon\). Therefore,
  \[
  f(\tau, b) \geq \frac{1}{2}\|\mu_*\|_K^2 - \frac{1}{2}(\xi + \varepsilon)^2 =: c_{\varepsilon,\xi} > 0 \quad\text{for all }(\tau,b)\in U,
  \]
  where positivity holds because \(\xi + \varepsilon < \|\mu_*\|_K\). From this point on, we proceed exactly as in the proof of Theorem~\ref{th:consistency-rates-h1}, obtaining \(\Pi_n(H_0|X_{1:n})=O_{\mathbb{P}_\mu*}(e^{-nc_{\varepsilon,\xi}/(1+\varepsilon)})\). Letting \(\varepsilon\to 0\) gives a constant \(\gamma\) in the exponent as close as desired to \(\frac{1}{2}(\|\mu_*\|_K^2 - \xi^2)\).

title: Proof\
body_md:
The first assertion in (i) is a consequence of the scalar law of large numbers applied entrywise. Alternatively, it can be immediately deduced from~\eqref{eq:uniform-consistency-empirical-covariance} by choosing the max-norm on matrices (since all matrix norms are equivalent):
  \[
  \|\hat{\mathbf C}_n - \mathbf K\|_{\max} = \max_{1\leq g,h\leq G} |\hat C_n(s_g, s_h) - K(s_g, s_h)| \leq \|\hat C_n - K\|_\infty \stackrel{\text{a.s.}}{\longrightarrow} 0.
  \]
  The second assertion is proven analogously.

  For (ii), note that \(\operatorname{Tr}(\cdot)\) is continuous, so from (i) we have
  \[
  \operatorname{Tr}(\hat{\mathbf C}_n) \stackrel{\text{a.s.}}{\longrightarrow} \operatorname{Tr}(\mathbf K)\quad \text{and}\quad \operatorname{Tr}(\hat{\mathbf C}_n^2) \stackrel{\text{a.s.}}{\longrightarrow} \operatorname{Tr}(\mathbf K^2).
  \]
  Then, the numerator in \(\hat\rho_n\), defined in~\eqref{eq:rho-oas}, converges almost surely to a finite positive constant (as long as \(G\geq 2\)). For the denominator, observe that
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:rho-oas-denominator-convergence}
    \operatorname{Tr}(\hat{\mathbf C}_n^2) - \frac{1}{G}\operatorname{Tr}^2(\hat{\mathbf C}_n) \stackrel{\text{a.s.}}{\longrightarrow} \operatorname{Tr}(\mathbf K^2) - \frac{1}{G}\operatorname{Tr}^2(\mathbf K).
  \end{equation}
  By Cauchy--Schwarz (using the definition of the trace as the sum of the eigenvalues), the right-hand side of~\eqref{eq:rho-oas-denominator-convergence} is always nonnegative, and it vanishes if and only if the true covariance matrix \(\mathbf K\) is spherical. Thus, we consider two cases:
  \begin{itemize}
  \item If, say, \(\mathbf K =\sigma^2 I_G\) with \(\sigma^2>0\), then the behavior of \(\hat \rho_n\) as \(n\to\infty\) is not easily determined (though it can be analyzed by a central limit theorem argument). Luckily this is irrelevant, since now both the empirical covariance and target covariance matrices converge a.s.\ to the same limit, namely \(\mathbf K\). Then,
  \[
  \|\hat{\mathbf K}_n^{\text{OAS}} - \mathbf K\| \leq (1-\hat\rho_n) \|\hat{\mathbf C}_n - \mathbf K\| + \hat\rho_n \left\|\frac{\operatorname{Tr}(\hat{\mathbf C}_n)}{G}I_G - \mathbf K\right\| \stackrel{\text{a.s.}}{\longrightarrow} 0.
  \]
  \item If \(\mathbf K\) is not spherical, then \(\|\operatorname{Tr}(\hat{\mathbf C}_n)I_G/G - \mathbf K\|\) converges to a finite constant almost surely. On the other hand, the denominator in~\eqref{eq:rho-oas} diverges almost surely as \(n\to\infty\), so \(\hat\rho_n\stackrel{\text{a.s.}}{\to} 0\). Then, using the same upper bound as in the previous case, we also get \(\|\hat{\mathbf K}_n^{\text{OAS}} - \mathbf K\|\to 0\) a.s.
  \end{itemize}

  We now prove the second assertion in (ii) in detail. The case \(p=1\) is trivial, so we assume \(p>1\). By the triangle inequality and particularizing to the Frobenius norm \(\|\cdot\|_F\), we have
  \[
  \sup_{\tau\in \mathcal C_p}\|\hat K^{\text{OAS}}_{n,\tau} - K_\tau\|_F \leq \sup_{\tau\in \mathcal C_p}\|\hat C_{n,\tau} - K_\tau\|_F + \sup_{\tau\in \mathcal C_p}\hat\rho_{n,\tau}\left\|\frac{\operatorname{Tr}(\hat C_{n,\tau})}{p}I_p - \hat C_{n,\tau}\right\|_F.
  \]
  The first term on the right-hand side goes to 0 almost surely by the uniform convergence established in (i). For the second term, let
  \[
  \hat{D}_{n,\tau} = \frac{\operatorname{Tr}(\hat C_{n,\tau})}{p}I_p - \hat C_{n,\tau},
  \]
  and note that \(\|\hat{D}_{n,\tau}\|_F^2 = \operatorname{Tr}(\hat D_{n,\tau}\hat D_{n,\tau}') = \operatorname{Tr}(\hat C_{n,\tau}^2) - \operatorname{Tr}^2(\hat C_{n,\tau})/p\). Then, for \(\tau\in \mathcal C_p\) we have
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:rho-frobenius-difference}
  \hat\rho_{n,\tau}\left\|\frac{\operatorname{Tr}(\hat C_{n,\tau})}{p}I_p - \hat C_{n,\tau}\right\|_F = \min\left\{1,\, \frac{\hat{N}_{n,\tau}}{(n + 1 - 2/p)\|\hat{D}_{n,\tau}\|_F^2}\right\}\|\hat{D}_{n,\tau}\|_F,
  \end{equation}
  where \(\hat{N}_{n,\tau} = (1-2/p) \operatorname{Tr}(\hat C_{n,\tau}^2) + \operatorname{Tr}^2(\hat C_{n,\tau}) \geq 0\). Now, for any \(A\geq 0\), \(c>0\) and \(x\geq 0\) the algebraic inequality \(\min\left\{1,\frac{A}{cx^2}\right\}x \leq \sqrt{\frac{A}{c}}\) holds (if \(x \leq \sqrt{A/c}\) the bound is trivial since the minimum is at most \(1\); if \(x > \sqrt{A/c}\) it evaluates to \(\frac{A}{cx^2}\), and in turn \(\frac{A}{cx^2}x < \sqrt{A/c}\)). Applying this bound to~\eqref{eq:rho-frobenius-difference} yields
  \[
  \hat\rho_{n,\tau}\|\hat D_{n,\tau}\|_F \leq \sqrt{\frac{\hat{N}_{n,\tau}}{n + 1 - 2/p}}.
  \]

  To conclude, we show that \(\hat N_{n,\tau}\) is uniformly bounded almost surely for large \(n\). To see this, define the continuous map \(F:\mathbb{R}^{p\times p} \to \mathbb{R}\) given by \(F(A)= (1-2/p)\operatorname{Tr}(A^2)+\operatorname{Tr}^2(A)\). Note that the set \(\{K_\tau: \tau \in \mathcal C_p\}\) is compact, so uniform convergence of \(\hat C_{n,\tau}\) to \(K_\tau\), given by (i), implies that for large \(n\) all \(\hat C_{n,\tau}\) lie almost surely in a fixed compact neighborhood of this set. The function \(F\) is uniformly continuous on this compact neighborhood, and therefore 
  \[
  \sup_{\tau\in \mathcal C_p}|F(\hat C_{n,\tau}) - F(K_\tau)| = \sup_{\tau\in \mathcal C_p}|\hat N_{n,\tau} - F(K_\tau)|\stackrel{\text{a.s.}}{\longrightarrow} 0.
  \] 
  This implies that \(\sup_{\tau\in \mathcal C_p}\hat N_{n,\tau}\leq \sup_{\tau\in \mathcal C_p} F(K_\tau)+ 1 =: M\) a.s.\ for all \(n\) large enough, and \(M<\infty\) by continuity. Hence,
  \[
  \sup_{\tau \in \mathcal C_p} \hat\rho_{n,\tau}\|\hat D_{n,\tau}\|_F \leq \sqrt{\frac{M}{n + 1 - 2/p}} \stackrel{\text{a.s.}}{\longrightarrow} 0.
  \]

label: eq:upper-bound-m-slab-plugin
title: Proof\
body_md:
We will follow the proof of Theorem~\ref{th:consistency-rates-h0} and adapt it only where necessary. First, observe that by~\ref{ass:compact-support-tau} and~\ref{ass:prior-p-finite} the sum \(\hat m_1(X_{1:n})\) reduces to
\[
\hat m_1(X_{1:n}) = \sum_{p=p_{\min}}^{P_{\max}} \Pi(p)\,\hat I_{n,p}(\mathcal C_p),
\]
where \(\hat I_{n,p}(\mathcal C_p)=\int_{\mathcal C_p}\hat m_{\text{slab}}(X_{1:n}|p,\tau)\Pi(\tau|p)\,d\tau\). Fix \(p_{\min} \leq p\leq P_{\max}\), and recall that there exists \(\lambda_p>0\) with \(\lambda_{\min}(K_\tau)\geq \lambda_p\) for all \(\tau\in \mathcal C_p\). By Weyl's inequality, choosing the spectral norm \(\|\cdot\|_2\) on matrices, we have
\[
\lambda_{\min}(\hat K_{n,\tau}) \geq \lambda_{\min}(K_\tau) - \|\hat K_{n,\tau} - K_\tau\|_2 \geq \lambda_p - \sup_{\tau\in \mathcal C_p}\|\hat K_{n,\tau} - K_\tau\|_2.
\]
Define the event where \(\hat K_{n,\tau}\) is uniformly close to \(K_\tau\) with a suitable bound, i.e.,
\[
F_n = \left\{\sup_{\tau\in \mathcal C_p}\|\hat K_{n,\tau} - K_\tau\|_2 \leq \frac{\lambda_p}{2}\right\},
\]
and note that \(\mathbb{P}_0(F_n^c)\to 0\) as \(n\to\infty\) by~\ref{ass:uniform-consistency-plug-in}. Furthermore, \(\lambda_{\min}(\hat K_{n,\tau})\geq \lambda_p/2\) for all \(\tau\in \mathcal C_p\) on \(F_n\), and consequently \(\lambda_{\min}(\hat\Lambda_{n,\tau})\geq n\lambda_p/2>0\). On \(F_n\), this yields the upper bound
\begin{equation}\label{eq:upper-bound-m-slab-plugin}
\hat m_{\text{slab}}(X_{1:n}|p,\tau) \leq \eta^{-p}\left(\frac{n\lambda_p}{2}\right)^{-p/2}\exp\left\{\frac{1}{n\lambda_p}\|S_n(\tau)\|^2\right\}, \quad \text{for all }\tau\in \mathcal C_p.
\end{equation}

Let \(\varepsilon>0\) and define the event \(E_{M}\) for a large enough \(M\) as in~\eqref{eq:event-E-n-M}, so that \(\mathbb{P}_0(E_M^c)<\varepsilon/2\). On the high-probability event \(F_n\cap E_{M}\), incorporating~\eqref{eq:upper-bound-m-slab-plugin} gives after integration
\[
\hat I_{n,p}(\mathcal C_p) \leq \eta^{-p}\left(\frac{n\lambda_p}{2}\right)^{-p/2}\exp\left\{\frac{M}{\lambda_p}\right\} =: \hat D\, n^{-p/2},
\]
where \(\hat D=\eta^{-p}(\lambda_p/2)^{-p/2}\exp\{M/\lambda_p\}\) is a finite constant independent of \(n\). Then, for sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
\mathbb{P}_0(\hat I_{n,p}(\mathcal C_p)>\hat D\, n^{-p/2}) \leq \mathbb{P}_0(F_n^c)+\mathbb{P}_0(E_{M}^c) < \varepsilon,
\]
showing \(\hat I_{n,p}(\mathcal C_p)=O_{\mathbb{P}_0}(n^{-p/2})\). Then, we conclude exactly as in the proof of Theorem~\ref{th:consistency-rates-h0}.

label: eq:plugin-f-lower-bound
title: Proof\
body_md:
We follow the proof strategy of Theorem~\ref{th:consistency-rates-h1}. Recover the approximating point \((p_\varepsilon,\tau_\varepsilon,b_\varepsilon)\), the compact neighborhood \(U=U_1\times U_2\) of \((\tau_\varepsilon, b_\varepsilon)\) with positive prior probability, and the function \(f(\tau, b)=\mu_*(\tau)'b - \frac{1}{2}b'K_\tau b\), which satisfies \(f(\tau, b)\geq \frac{1}{2}\|\mu_*\|_K^2 - 2\varepsilon^2 >0\) for all \((\tau,b)\in U\) and sufficiently small \(\varepsilon>0\). Define the plug-in analogue
\[
\hat f_n(\tau,b) = \mu_*(\tau)'b - \frac{1}{2}b'\hat K_{n,\tau} b,\quad \text{for all } (\tau,b)\in U,
\]
and bound the plug-in error by
\[
\sup_{(\tau,b)\in U}|\hat f_n(\tau,b) - f(\tau,b)| = \sup_{(\tau,b)\in U}\frac{1}{2}|b'(\hat K_{n,\tau}-K_\tau)b| \leq \frac{B^2}{2}\sup_{\tau\in U_1}\|\hat K_{n,\tau}-K_\tau\|_2,
\]
where \(0<B=\sup_{b\in U_2} \|b\|<\infty\) and \(\|\cdot\|_2\) is the spectral norm on matrices. Now, define the event 
\[
G_n = \left\{\sup_{\tau\in U_1}\|\hat K_{n,\tau} - K_\tau\|_2 \leq \frac{2\varepsilon^2}{B^2}\right\}.
\]
On the one hand, by~\ref{ass:uniform-consistency-plug-in} we have \(\mathbb{P}_{\mu_*}(G_n^c)\to 0\) as \(n\to\infty\). On the other hand, on \(G_n\),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:plugin-f-lower-bound}
\hat f_n(\tau,b) \geq f(\tau,b) - \varepsilon^2 \geq \frac{1}{2}\|\mu_*\|_K^2 - 3\varepsilon^2 =: d_\varepsilon, \quad \text{for all } (\tau,b)\in U,
\end{equation}
where \(d_\varepsilon>0\) can be achieved by taking \(\varepsilon\) small enough. In this case, the plug-in log-likelihood for \(p_\varepsilon\) and \((\tau, b)\in U\) becomes
\begin{equation}\label{eq:log-likelihood-plugin}
\log \hat L(X_{1:n}|p_\varepsilon, \tau, b) = n\mu_*(\tau)'b - \frac{n}{2}b'\hat K_{n,\tau}b + \sqrt{n}Z_\tau' b = n\hat f_n(\tau, b) + \sqrt{n}Z_\tau' b,
\end{equation}
where \(Z_\tau = \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}(S_n(\tau) - n\mu_*(\tau))\). Moreover, recall that by Cauchy--Schwarz we have
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cauchy-schwarz-plugin}
\sqrt{n} Z_\tau' b \geq -\sqrt{n} B \sup_{\tau \in U_1}\|Z_\tau\|.
\end{equation}

On \(G_n\), restricting the domain of integration and using~\eqref{eq:plugin-f-lower-bound},~\eqref{eq:log-likelihood-plugin} and~\eqref{eq:cauchy-schwarz-plugin} produces the bound
\begin{equation}\label{eq:lower-bound-m1-plugin}
  \begin{split}
  \hat m_1(X_{1:n}) &\geq \Pi(p_\varepsilon)\int_{U_1}\int_{U_2}\mathcal N_{p_\varepsilon}(b|0,\eta^2 I_{p_\varepsilon})\exp\left\{n\hat f_n(\tau,b)+\sqrt{n} Z_\tau'b\right\}\Pi(\tau|p_\varepsilon)\,db\,d\tau \\
  &\geq D\exp\left\{nd_\varepsilon - \sqrt{n}\,B\cdot\sup_{\tau\in U_1}\|Z_\tau\|\right\},
  \end{split}
\end{equation}
where \(D=\Pi(p_\varepsilon)\Pi_\tau(U_1|p_{\varepsilon})\Pi_b^{\text{slab}}(U_2|p_{\varepsilon})>0\) by assumption. Now, since \(Z_\tau \sim \mathcal N_{p_\varepsilon}(0, K_\tau)\) under \(H_1\), we already saw in the proof of Theorem~\ref{th:consistency-rates-h1} that for any \(\delta>0\) there exists \(M>0\) such that the event
\[
H_M = \left\{B\cdot \sup_{\tau\in U_1}\|Z_\tau\| \leq M\right\}
\]
satisfies \(\mathbb{P}_{\mu_*}(H_M^c)<\delta/2\). Thus, we have the inequality \(\hat m_1(X_{1:n}) \geq D\exp\{nd_\varepsilon - \sqrt{n}M\}\) on \(G_n\cap H_M\) by~\eqref{eq:lower-bound-m1-plugin}. Since \(nd_\varepsilon/(1+\varepsilon)\) grows slower than \(nd_\varepsilon - \sqrt{n}M\) as \(n\to\infty\), for sufficiently large \(n\) we obtain \(\hat m_1(X_{1:n}) \geq D\exp\{n d_\varepsilon/(1+\varepsilon)\}\) on \(G_n\cap H_M\). Therefore,
\[
\hat\Pi_n(H_0|X_{1:n}) = \frac{\pi_0}{\pi_0+(1-\pi_0)\hat m_1(X_{1:n})}\leq \frac{\pi_0}{(1-\pi_0)\hat m_1(X_{1:n})}\leq \tilde{D}\exp\left\{\frac{-nd_\varepsilon}{1+\varepsilon}\right\}
\]
on \(G_n\cap H_M\), where \(\tilde{D}=\pi_0/((1-\pi_0)D)\). Write \(\mathbb{P}_{\mu_*}(G_n^c\cup H_M^c)\leq \mathbb{P}_{\mu_*}(G_n^c)+\mathbb{P}_{\mu_*}(H_M^c)\), and note that the first term vanishes as \(n\to\infty\), while the second is at most \(\delta/2\). Then, for sufficiently large \(n\) we have proved that
\[
\mathbb{P}_{\mu_*}\left(\hat\Pi_n(H_0|X_{1:n})>\tilde{D}\exp\{-nd_\varepsilon/(1+\varepsilon)\}\right)<\delta,
\]
so \(\hat\Pi_n(H_0|X_{1:n})=O_{\mathbb{P}_{\mu_*}}(e^{-nd_\varepsilon/(1+\varepsilon)})\) and, as before, \(\lim_{\varepsilon\to 0}\, d_\varepsilon/(1+\varepsilon)=\frac{1}{2}\|\mu_*\|_K^2\). The proof of the second part of the theorem is almost identical, except that \(f(\tau,b)\) is lower bounded by \(c_{\varepsilon,\xi}\) as in the construction from the proof of Theorem~\ref{th:consistency-rates-h1-alt}.

label: lem:expectation-identity
title: Lemma
body_md: \label{lem:expectation-identity} For any \((p, \tau)\in \mathbb{N} \times \mathcal T_p\) and every \(n\geq 1\), we have \(\mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{P}_0}[m_{\emph{slab}}(X_{1:n}|p,\tau)] = 1\).

label: eq:type-ii-error-bound
title: Proof\
body_md:
Suppose by contradiction that a faster rate holds, say \(\Pi_n(H_0|X_{1:n})=O_{\mathbb{P}_{\mu_*}}(e^{-n\zeta})\) for \(\zeta > \frac{1}{2}\|\mu_*\|_K^2\). By definition, for any \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\) there exists \(M>0\) such that the region
  \[
  R_n = \{X_{1:n}: \Pi_n(H_0|X_{1:n}) \leq M e^{-n\zeta}\}
  \]
  satisfies \(\mathbb{P}_{\mu_*}(R_n)> 1-\varepsilon\) for sufficiently large \(n\). Then, reusing the notation \(m_1(X_{1:n})\) from~\eqref{eq:posterior-slab-m1}, on \(R_n\) we have 
  \[
  \Pi_n(H_0|X_{1:n}) = \frac{\pi_0}{\pi_0 + (1-\pi_0)m_1(X_{1:n})} \leq M e^{-n\zeta},
  \]
  and rearranging yields
  \[
  \pi_0(1-M e^{-n\zeta}) \leq (1-\pi_0)m_1(X_{1:n}) M e^{-n\zeta}.
  \]
  For sufficiently large \(n\) we have \(1-M e^{-n\zeta} \geq 1/2\), so eventually we get
  \[
  1\leq \frac{2M(1-\pi_0)}{\pi_0} e^{-n\zeta} m_1(X_{1:n}).
  \]
  Integrating on \(R_n\) on both sides with respect to \(\mathbb{P}_0\) and using the fact that \(m_1(X_{1:n})\) is a valid marginal likelihood (it integrates to 1 under \(\mathbb{P}_0\) over the whole space by Lemma~\ref{lem:expectation-identity}), we have
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:type-ii-error-bound}
  \mathbb{P}_0(R_n) \leq \frac{2M(1-\pi_0)}{\pi_0} e^{-n\zeta} \int_{R_n} m_1(X_{1:n})\, d\mathbb{P}_0 \leq C e^{-n\zeta}\quad \text{for large } n,
  \end{equation}
  where \(C>0\) is a constant. Now we construct a frequentist test \(\phi_n\) for the reverse hypotheses \(\tilde{H}_0: \mu\equiv \mu_*\) against \(\tilde{H}_1: \mu\equiv 0\), given by \(\phi_n(X_{1:n}) = \mathds{1}\{X_{1:n} \in R_n^c\}\). In this case, according to~\eqref{eq:rn-derivative} the Kullback--Leibler divergence from \(\mathbb{P}_{\mu_*}\) to \(\mathbb{P}_0\) is
  \[
  \operatorname{D_{KL}}(\mathbb{P}_{\mu_*} \,\|\, \mathbb{P}_0) = \mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{P}_{\mu_*}}\left[\log \frac{d\mathbb{P}_{\mu_*}}{d\mathbb{P}_0}(X)\right] = \mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{P}_{\mu_*}}[\left\langleX,\mu_*\right\rangle_K] - \frac{1}{2}\|\mu_*\|^2_K = \frac{1}{2}\|\mu_*\|_K^2,
  \]
  where we used the equivalence \(\mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{P}_{\mu_*}}[\left\langleX,\mu_*\right\rangle_K]=\left\langle\mu_*,\mu_*\right\rangle_K=\|\mu_*\|_K^2\) that stems from Loève's isometry \citep[p.~974]{parzen1961approach}. For sufficiently large \(n\), the type I error probability is bounded, since \(\mathbb{P}_{\mu_*}(\phi_n = 1)=\mathbb{P}_{\mu_*}(R_n^c) < \varepsilon\). On the other hand, by~\eqref{eq:type-ii-error-bound} the type II error probability for large \(n\) is \(\mathbb{P}_0(\phi_n=0)=\mathbb{P}_0(R_n)\leq C e^{-n\zeta}\), which decays exponentially with exponential constant greater than \(\operatorname{D_{KL}}(\mathbb{P}_{\mu_*} \,\|\, \mathbb{P}_0)\), contradicting Chernoff--Stein.
